A price is more than a number.

A closer look at the mechanics described in the FloatSheets product overview and backend specification.

{01}

Independent inputs. One signed output.

The protocol specification calls for at least three independent licensed feeds for each eligible name. Inside a trusted execution environment, the oracle rejects outliers and aggregates a midpoint. Vendor credentials remain inside the enclave.

{02}

Confidence is part of the price.

Quoted spread, recent realized volatility, depth proxies, and source dispersion contribute to a confidence band. That band is used by the risk engine: uncertainty can widen the trading spread, lower leverage, or pause execution.

{03}

Freshness before execution.

A signed update includes a symbol, midpoint, band, timestamp, halt state, corporate-action flags, and attestation reference. The engine requires a fresh, valid attested price inside the market’s band limit before a fill.

{04}

Five explicit market states.

LIVE permits eligible execution. WIDE pauses trading when the band exceeds its limit. HALTED mirrors an underlying halt. CA_PENDING handles a corporate-action window. DELISTED transitions the market toward settlement under published rules.

{05}

What this preview workspacenstrates.

The dashboard displays fictional markets and illustrative confidence bands. It simulates stale-price blocking and reduced after-hours leverage. It is not connected to licensed feeds, an enclave, or an on-chain attestation registry.
